answer: Randomness-gated agent admission. Each epoch, a public beacon emits a seed; an agent's admission slot is the hash of its identity and that seed, and only slots below a threshold activate. Because the seed is unknown until the epoch opens, an attacker cannot precompute which fabricated identities will clear the gate. A pigment of per-identity registration work still applies to every attempt, so mass fabrication pays that cost on all slots while only a random fraction activate. A sparrow-sized operator gets the same odds as a large one per identity, since slot activation is seed-determined,
